title: Speaking & Writing
subject: Bahasa Inggris
prerequisites: Peserta didik telah mempelajari kosakata tambahan tentang kegiatan di waktu luang dan memahami teks undangan pesta ulang tahun.
resources: Sumber Belajar:  Rise Up! Teens! Student Book 1, page 62-63
Laptop/ komputer, pengeras suara, projector, PPT
learningModel: Discovery Learning, Task-Based Learning, Tatap Muka.
approach: Peserta didik diajak untuk fokus dan saksama saat menyimak audio, mengamati detail gambar/komik, dan memperhatikan struktur bahasa yang digunakan.
Peserta didik menghubungkan materi pembelajaran dengan pengalaman dan kehidupan nyata mereka, sehingga pembelajaran terasa relevan dan bermanfaat.
Pembelajaran dikemas dalam aktivitas yang menyenangkan seperti permainan tebak hobi, kerja kelompok, penggunaan komik strip, dan survei interaktif.
objectives: Learners will be able to speak and write about which activities people prefer to do and why, using would prefer to / would rather and because.
Learners will reflect on their own favorite activities and learn why it is important to keep going with something, even when it’s difficult (perseverance).

details: Greet the students and ask about their feelings. For example: “How are you feeling today?” or “How would you describe your mood in one word?”
Play a quick “This or That” game to review the unit vocabulary: the teacher says two activities (e.g. “play volleyball or go swimming?”) and points to two sides of the classroom.
Students move to (or point to) the side of the activity they like more. Ask 1-2 students on each side to say their choice in a full sentence.
Other alternatives to warm up the class: hot potato and throw the ball.
Ask students to look at Student Book page 62.
First, the teacher reads the questions in the speech bubble at the top of the page aloud for the students to hear.
Next, the teacher asks everyone to read the questions aloud as a class.
Then, ask students to ask and answer the questions, in pairs.

Model to the students how the questions can be changed by changing some of the key vocabulary in the questions, e.g. “Would you prefer to watch a concert or go to the mall?” → “Would you rather watch a movie or play volleyball?”

Now, put them in different pairs and ask them to substitute some of the key vocabulary in the questions so they can practice asking about different activities. This can be repeated several times by putting students into different pairs.
To finish the speaking activity, elicit responses from some students by asking the questions in the speech bubbles with the original vocabulary, and also with some substituted vocabulary.

Check the Teacher’s Guide to see further explanation about the Language Box (meaning, form, use, common mistakes, e.g. “I would rather to watch a movie” and “I would prefer to going swimming”). This can be used to help answer students' questions.

Ask students to look at the Speaking and Writing B task on Student Book page 62 and check if students understand the task, e.g., Which activity are we doing? What page is it on? What do you have to do?
Put students in groups of three. Each student asks questions 1-4 to both of their partners and asks them to give a reason using because.
They should write their partners' answers in the space provided in the Student Book, not their own.

Read the model answers aloud together as a class, e.g. “I would rather play VR games because they are more exciting.” and “I would prefer to go to the mall because I want to buy a new T-shirt.” Remind students that would prefer is followed by to + verb, but would rather is followed by the base verb only.
After 10-15 minutes, elicit some answers from each group. Answers will vary because they are students’ own personal responses.
This is an additional activity for further practice if there is time.
Ask students to write three of their own questions in their notebooks, following the format on the page: “Would you prefer to … or …? Why?” or “Would you rather … or …? Why?”
Give students 3-4 minutes to write their questions.
Then, put students in pairs and ask them to practice asking and answering the questions. Students write their partner’s answers in their notebooks.
Ask students to find a new partner and repeat the activity.
Finally, elicit some questions and answers from several pairs of students.
Direct the students to look at the picture on page 63 and ask them “What can you see on the page?” to elicit some answers.

Next, tell students to read the text about the Teen Value (perseverance and the importance of hobbies). They can read it silently, or put them in pairs to share reading the text aloud together, sentence by sentence.
Elicit from students, “What is the key focus of this Teen Corner page?”, and “Why do you think this skill (or value) is important?”
Ask students to look at activity A and read the instructions as given on the page. Ask some instruction-checking questions to check if students understand the task.
Ask students if they know the story “The Tortoise and the Hare”. Elicit what the story is about.

Ask students to read activity A on their own or with a partner. Teachers can also divide the class into groups or rows and ask each group to read a few sentences alternately, from the first to the last sentence.
Ask a few comprehension questions to check understanding, e.g. “Who was faster?” and “What did the hare do during the race?”
Ask students to look at activity B and read the instructions as given on the page.

Put students into groups of 3-4 and ask them to read and discuss the questions, e.g. “Why didn’t the hare win the race?”, “How did the tortoise show perseverance?”, “What does perseverance mean to you?”
Give about 6-8 minutes to complete this task.
Elicit answers from each group for each question, e.g. “The tortoise won because he kept going and didn’t stop.”
Ask students to look at activity C and read the instructions as given on the page.
In groups of 3 or 4, students choose one hobby to focus on (e.g. playing the guitar, swimming, drawing).
Students discuss three challenges people face when learning this hobby, then make a “Perseverance Power-Up Plan”, give advice for a beginner, and explain how small steps help someone improve.
Show and read the model answer together as a class (Hobby: Playing the Guitar – “I can practise a little every day and keep going when it’s difficult.”) so students can see what they need to do.
Ask each group to present their plan to the class. Each person in the group should speak (Student A presents number 1, Student B number 2, and so on).
If there isn’t enough time, groups can finish their plan and present it at the beginning of the next lesson.
Wrap up the class by highlighting that hobbies can be difficult at first, but practicing a little every day and not giving up, like the tortoise, helps us improve.
Conclude the lesson, give feedback, and appreciation toward the student(s) / the whole class. Dismiss the class.

assessment: Asesmen formatif: unjuk kerja speaking berpasangan (kelancaran, ketepatan, keberanian).
Produk tulisan sederhana sesuai model di Student Book (struktur & kosakata unit).
Umpan balik teman sebaya dan guru terhadap hasil speaking/writing.
reflectionStudent: Apa hal baru yang kamu pelajari hari ini?
Bagian mana yang paling mudah dan paling sulit bagimu? Mengapa?
Kalimat bahasa Inggris apa yang sudah bisa kamu ucapkan dengan percaya diri?
Apa yang akan kamu lakukan untuk berlatih di rumah?
reflectionTeacher: Apakah tujuan pembelajaran tercapai? Bukti apa yang menunjukkannya?
Kegiatan mana yang paling efektif dan mana yang perlu diperbaiki?
Berapa persen instruksi kelas yang disampaikan dalam bahasa Inggris?
Peserta didik mana yang memerlukan pendampingan atau pengayaan?
